es: Interpretar gráficos de asistencia, pasos y temperaturas: reconocer verbos de tendencia, cifras aproximadas y proporciones.

teaching.en: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily from 400 to 900 over the whole season, without a single sharp drop along the way.
teaching.es: Como muestra el gráfico, la asistencia subió de forma constante de 400 a 900 a lo largo de toda la temporada, sin una sola caída brusca en el camino.
teaching.explanationEs: As the chart shows abre la descripción; rose steadily dice que subió sin saltos; from… to… da el inicio y el final.
segments: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily from 400 to 900 over
the whole season, without a single sharp drop along the way.
teaching.audioText: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily from 400 to 900 over the whole season, without a single sharp drop along the way.

teaching.en: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June, and that month turned out to be the peak of the entire year.
teaching.es: Los pasos diarios subieron bruscamente un 20 % en junio, y ese mes resultó ser el punto máximo de todo el año.
teaching.explanationEs: By + cifra dice cuánto cambió (en español «en un 20 %»). Peak es el punto más alto de la línea.
segments: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June, and that
month turned out to be the peak of the entire year.
teaching.audioText: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June, and that month turned out to be the peak of the entire year.

teaching.en: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees throughout the spring, so it would be misleading to claim that there is a clear trend.
teaching.es: Las temperaturas fluctúan entre 12 y 18 grados durante toda la primavera, así que sería engañoso afirmar que hay una tendencia clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Fluctuate describe una línea en zigzag; trend es la dirección general de la línea.
segments: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees throughout the spring, so it
would be misleading to claim that there is a clear trend.
teaching.audioText: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees throughout the spring, so it would be misleading to claim that there is a clear trend.

teaching.en: Roughly two thirds of the fans come by bus, which means that the majority of them travel together to every match.
teaching.es: Aproximadamente dos tercios de los aficionados vienen en autobús, lo que significa que la mayoría viaja junta a cada partido.
teaching.explanationEs: Roughly suaviza la cifra porque no es exacta. Majority significa más de la mitad, y dos tercios la superan.
segments: Roughly two thirds of the fans come by bus, which means
that the majority of them travel together to every match.
teaching.audioText: Roughly two thirds of the fans come by bus, which means that the majority of them travel together to every match.

teaching.en: Only a quarter of the students walk to school, and that proportion has stayed in the region of twenty-five percent during the last five years.
teaching.es: Solo una cuarta parte de los estudiantes va andando al colegio, y esa proporción se ha mantenido en torno al veinticinco por ciento durante los últimos cinco años.
teaching.explanationEs: A quarter es el 25 %. Proportion es la parte que algo representa dentro del total; in the region of significa «alrededor de».
segments: Only a quarter of the students walk to school, and that proportion has
stayed in the region of twenty-five percent during the last five years.
teaching.audioText: Only a quarter of the students walk to school, and that proportion has stayed in the region of twenty-five percent during the last five years.

teaching.en: After the summer surge, visitor numbers began to plateau, or level off, and the two busiest months account for nearly half of the yearly total.
teaching.es: Tras el aumento repentino del verano, el número de visitantes empezó a estabilizarse (plateau, o level off), y los dos meses más concurridos representan casi la mitad del total anual.
teaching.explanationEs: Surge es una subida repentina; plateau o level off, dejar de subir; account for + fracción dice qué parte del total representa algo.
segments: After the summer surge, visitor numbers began to plateau, or level off, and
the two busiest months account for nearly half of the yearly total.
teaching.audioText: After the summer surge, visitor numbers began to plateau, or level off, and the two busiest months account for nearly half of the yearly total.

prompt.es: Lee la nota del entrenador y elige qué línea describe la asistencia.

choices.text: It rose steadily, peaked in March and then dropped sharply for good.
It climbed without jumps, reached a peak and then went up and down.
It rose sharply, peaked in March and then moved up and down.

feedback.es: La nota dice que la asistencia subió de forma constante hasta marzo y luego fluctuó entre 600 y 700, sin una tendencia clara.

hint.es: Fíjate en qué hace la línea primero (steadily) y en qué hace después (fluctuate).

origin.text: Coach's note: 'Attendance rose steadily until March, when roughly 900 fans came to the match. After that, the numbers began to fluctuate between 600 and 700, so I cannot see a clear trend for the rest of the season.'

prompt.es: Completa: «La proporción de estudiantes que van en bici sigue siendo una cuarta parte.»

feedback.es: Proportion es la parte que algo representa dentro del total; aquí cambia el número de ciclistas, pero no su parte del total.

hint.es: Es la parte que algo representa dentro del total, no una cifra absoluta.

origin.text: Last year 240 of 960 students cycled to school, and this year 250 of 1,000 do. The ___ of students who cycle has hardly changed: it is still one quarter.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los dos meses más concurridos representan casi la mitad del total anual.»

answer.text: The two busiest months account for nearly half of the yearly total

feedback.es: Account for + fracción dice qué parte del total representa algo; el sujeto plural (months) pide account, sin -s.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto: los dos meses más concurridos.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo evolucionó el número de visitantes del parque.

choices.text: A slow rise in the spring, a drop in July and then a flatter line.
A steady rise that ended in July and was followed by a sharp drop.
A steady rise, a sudden jump in July and then a flatter line.

feedback.es: El audio habla de una subida constante en primavera, una surge en julio y después una estabilización (level off).

origin.audio: Here is what the chart tells us about the park. Visitor numbers climbed slowly but surely through the spring, and then there was a surge in July, when a big crowd came in a single week. Since then the line has stayed flat, and most of the visitors now arrive at the weekend.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase sobre el gráfico con su traducción natural.

pairs.es: Las ventas se dispararon en junio.
Los precios se estabilizaron en julio.

pairs: Rent accounts for half of my costs.

pairs.es: El alquiler representa la mitad de mis gastos.
Las cifras suben y bajan todo el año.

feedback.es: Cada expresión describe un movimiento distinto: subida repentina, estabilización, parte del total y zigzag.

pairs.es: Las ventas se dispararon en junio.
Los precios se estabilizaron en julio.

pairs: Rent accounts for half of my costs.

pairs.es: El alquiler representa la mitad de mis gastos.
Las cifras suben y bajan todo el año.

prompt.es: Completa: «La asistencia subió de forma constante de 400 en enero a 900 en marzo.»

feedback.es: Rose steadily describe una subida constante, sin saltos ni caídas, como la de esta línea de enero a marzo.

origin.text: The report covers the whole season. Attendance rose ___ from 400 in January to 900 in March, with no sudden jumps and no falls along the way.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe del club y elige qué opina la tesorera sobre la bajada.

choices.text: That a few weeks of exams explain most of the fall in numbers.
That a quarter of the fans have stopped coming to the big matches.
That the fall shows that members are losing interest in the club.

feedback.es: La tesorera atribuye la mayor parte de la bajada a dos semanas de exámenes, es decir, a una causa temporal y no a un desinterés general.

origin.audio: In our club's yearly review, the chart is clear about one thing: attendance rose steadily for four months, peaked in March, and then began to rise and fall. Some members say the club is losing interest, but the treasurer is more cautious. She points out that most of the drop comes from two weeks of exams, when far fewer students could attend. A quarter of the fans, she adds, come only for the big matches, so a single figure can hide very different habits.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué da a entender la tesorera sobre las cifras.

choices.text: That the big matches are the only games that really matter to the fans.
That one overall number can hide very different ways of attending.
That most fans would come more often if the tickets were cheaper.

feedback.es: Al decir que una sola cifra puede esconder hábitos muy distintos, la tesorera advierte contra sacar conclusiones de un único dato.

origin.audio: In our club's yearly review, the chart is clear about one thing: attendance rose steadily for four months, peaked in March, and then began to rise and fall. Some members say the club is losing interest, but the treasurer is more cautious. She points out that most of the drop comes from two weeks of exams, when far fewer students could attend. A quarter of the fans, she adds, come only for the big matches, so a single figure can hide very different habits.

prompt.es: Completa: «Este año las cifras fluctúan tanto que no hay tendencia clara.»

feedback.es: Fluctuate describe un zigzag que impide ver una tendencia; vary sería una alternativa igual de válida.

origin.text: Unlike last year, when the line rose steadily, this year's numbers ___ so much that nobody can identify a clear trend. The committee therefore prefers to wait for the next report.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso de la liga y elige qué da a entender el comité.

choices.text: That the drop is lasting, so the schedule must change now.
That exams are certainly the cause of the whole fall in numbers.
That the drop may be temporary, so no action is needed yet.

feedback.es: El comité condiciona cualquier cambio a que la bajada continúe en mayo: por ahora la considera posiblemente temporal.

origin.text: Note from the league office: 'Match attendance fell from 900 in March to 640 in April, but two of the April games were held on exam days. Unless the fall continues in May, the committee will not change the schedule.'

prompt.es: Lee el extracto del informe y elige qué actitud muestra ante la cifra de 9.000.

choices.text: Cautious: the headline figure hides a minority who walk much less.
Enthusiastic: the June peak proves that all the staff now walk much more.
Dismissive: the figure says nothing because a minority walk little.

feedback.es: El informe celebra el máximo de junio pero recuerda que una cuarta parte del personal anda poco: es una postura prudente, no triunfalista.

origin.text: Extract from the clinic's report: 'Daily steps among workers rose steadily to a peak of 9,000 in June. However, a quarter of the staff still recorded fewer than 4,000, so the overall figure should be read with care.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuándo se concentró la mayoría de los días más calurosos.

choices.text: In the first half of July.
In the second half of July.
Throughout the spring, when temperatures fluctuated.

feedback.es: Dos tercios de los días más calurosos cayeron en las dos últimas semanas de julio, tras el máximo de 26 grados.

origin.audio: Temperatures fluctuated between twelve and eighteen degrees in spring, then rose sharply to peak at twenty-six in July. About two thirds of the hottest days fell in the last two weeks of that month.

prompt.es: Completa: «La encuesta cubrió 2.000 hogares y aproximadamente 1.200 notaron una subida.»

feedback.es: Roughly antes de una cifra indica que es aproximada; approximately, about o around funcionan igual.

origin.text: The survey covered 2,000 homes. ___ 1,200 of them reported a rise in their bills, while the others saw no change at all.
